title: After ProPublica Investigation, House Democrats Demand Answers on U.S. Citizens Detained by Immigration Agents
author: Nicole Foy
content:
**What Happened:** Citing [ProPublica’s recent
investigation](https://projects.propublica.org/american-citizens-detained-dhs-
civil-rights/), House Democrats are [again
asking](https://www.propublica.org/article/immigration-ice-americans-detained-
joint-congressional-investigation) the Trump administration to explain why
hundreds of U.S. citizens have been held by immigration agents and how the
government verifies citizenship during immigration operations.

In [an October
letter](https://correa.house.gov/imo/media/doc/letter_dhs_immigration_enforcement_and_us_citizens1.pdf)
to Department of Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, California Rep.
Lou Correa and 39 other legislators demanded the administration share the
number of citizens that immigration agents have detained and how the
government is tracking such encounters. They also asked for more information
about how agents are trained to verify citizenship and legal status.

**Why It Matters:** ProPublica counted more than 500 Americans detained by
immigration agents — almost certainly an undercount since the government is
not transparently tracking the cases.

Experts told us the cases collectively show federal agents running roughshod
over the constitutional rights of citizens. We found more than 100 Americans
who were questioned about their citizenship, 63 Americans detained while
recording, 36 Americans held for at least a day without being able to contact
a lawyer or their family and roughly a dozen citizens deported, mostly
children.

**What They Said:** “We remain concerned that the Department’s actions are
violating American citizens’ constitutional rights to due process, equal
protection, and freedom from unreasonable search and seizure, and request
transparency regarding the Department’s actions,” the representatives wrote in
their letter to DHS.

DHS has long insisted it is not arresting U.S. citizens, and it defended its
immigration operations as “highly targeted.”

“These members of Congress have shown more concern for criminal illegal aliens
who’ve broken our laws and destroyed any possibility of ever remaining in our
country than they ever have for Rachel Morin, Laken Riley, Jocelyn Nungaray,
and the true victims of illegal alien crimes in America,” a spokesperson wrote
to ProPublica.

**Background:** Democrats have been pushing the second Trump administration
for more details about how immigration agents are interacting with U.S.
citizens [since early 2025](https://www.propublica.org/article/trump-ice-
immigration-detained-americans-congress-questions-unanswered). Last year,
congressional Democrats [announced a wide-ranging investigation into
immigration agents’ detention of U.S.
citizens](https://www.propublica.org/article/immigration-ice-americans-
detained-joint-congressional-investigation) in response to our earlier
reporting that found that [more than 170 citizens were detained by immigration
agents](https://www.propublica.org/article/immigration-dhs-american-citizens-
arrested-detained-against-will).

Last month, Rep. Teresa Leger Fernández, a New Mexico Democrat, introduced a
bill, Justice for Citizens Wrongfully Detained by ICE Act, that would [make it
easier for citizens to sue immigration
agents](https://www.propublica.org/article/american-citizens-wrongfully-
detained-ice-bill) for wrongful arrests.
